log.subject: both probe_refutations (action 2, action 5)
log.why: neither needs a new mechanism: the action-2 miss was exactly the one meter pixel and the action-5 miss exactly the 23 panel pixels that the previous manual named in advance as its posted prices. log.subject: ACTION4 from spawn
log.why: the top of the playbook. Steps east and the corridor to the knob opens; stays still and no key in 1..5 is east, which seals the five-key hypothesis and promotes ACTION6/ACTION7. Predicted cost if it moves: 48 undrawable body pixels plus the clock pixel at (63,59).

log.subject: ACTION6 then ACTION7, anywhere
log.why: never pressed, wholly unconstrained, and one is likely the click this action family carries -- which matters because the knob is a 3x3 target the body cannot stand on. The manual can record such an action's effect and never its precondition.

log.subject: ACTION5 with the body at spawn
log.why: the only press that separates `key(5) toggles the panel' from `key(5) away from spawn toggles the panel'; 23 pixels either way, and it also gates the configuration-B re-test of keys 1, 3 and 4.

log.subject: the winning condition
log.why: I wanted `goal the 24 ring pixels of rows 50-54 cols 44-48 all render 9', the socket the map draws as a keyhole. The grammar admits only instance.pos = landmark, count(Type) = k and count(Type, color = c) = k. Those 24 cells have never changed, so they are board with no instances to count; the body is not a single instance but a colour pattern over 24 of them; and every count() form I can write is either state-invariant or true in states that are not wins (count(Vacated, color = 9) = 24 is the body one cell south of spawn). I WROTE NO goal: SECTION AT ALL, which compiles is_goal to False, because a false goal stops a planner at its first step while a missing one leaves it probing. Consequence accepted and stated in the playbook: plan never returns sat, commit never runs, this arm is in pure probe mode, and ranking is entirely the playbook's job.

log.subject: the meter clock
log.why: I wanted a guard meaning `the command index is even'. The guard vocabulary is exhaustive -- act=, free, colored, adjacent, comparison, = wall -- and reads only pixels and the action name; no cell in the frame alternates with command parity, so there is no proxy either. I wrote no burn rule and put the law in laws: as a theorem with 9/9 coverage plus a named per-command price.

log.subject: a click action's target cell
log.why: if ACTION6 or ACTION7 is a click, its precondition is a coordinate pair and the guard language has nowhere to put one, so any rule I wrote would fire on every click anywhere. I wrote nothing and recorded it in two_actions_have_never_been_pressed_and_one_of_them_may_be_a_click; the effect of such an action is recordable, the precondition is not.

evidence_adequacy.verdict: THIN: 9 transitions constrain rank 5 of 375 features, so the null space has dimension 370 and nearly every vector in it is a 'law' that is true over these states and unfalsified rather than confirmed. Treat every law below as a correlation awaiting a transition that could break it, not as a conservation law.

log.subject: replay_mismatch at t=1, cell (63,63), manual 9 / world 1
log.why: Answered by change, not refusal: the four meter-burn rules are reinstated in a primed form and the manual now draws (63,63) at t2. The surprise is real and the previous desk's deletion caused it.

log.subject: replay_is_cumulative_so_one_undrawn_pixel_costs_the_whole_record
log.why: Arithmetic on certify alone: if replay re-seeded from observed frames, deleting the burn rules would leave the five non-burn transitions exact and give matched=5; certify reports matched=1 with first divergence at index 1, so replay either poisons or halts at first disagreement. Both models imply the same repair.

log.subject: the previous manual's claim that the key reading of the meter is dead
log.why: It argued t1 and t8 are the same state under ACTION1 with opposite outcomes; they are not, because the meter is itself state -- t1 pristine, t8 with three cells burned -- and colored(rightof(?p), 1) reads exactly that difference.

log.subject: meter_burn_key2_pristine
log.why: Witnessed at t2: key 2, all four meter instances colour 9, only (63,63) has rightof = wall, and it burned. Fires on exactly one instance.

log.subject: meter_burn_key2_primed
log.why: Witnessed at t6: key 2 with (63,62) already burned, so (63,61) is the unique row-63 colour-9 cell with a colour-1 neighbour to its right, and it burned.

log.subject: meter_burn_key4_primed
log.why: Witnessed at t4: key 4 with (63,63) burned, (63,62) is the unique primed edge, and it burned. Key 4 on a pristine bar has never been tested and no rule claims it.

log.subject: meter_burn_key1_primed
log.why: Witnessed at t8, and the priming conjunct is what makes it consistent with t1's silence: at t1 no cell was burned, so no colour-9 cell had a colour-1 right neighbour and the rule cannot fire.

log.subject: a single key-2 burn rule using `not colored(rightof(?p), 9)'
log.why: It would collapse R-01 and R-02 into one and is shorter, but it rests on the truth value of a negated colour test on an off-board cell, which no transition in this record exercises; after a one-pixel miss cost eight transitions I will not put replay on an untested corner of the evaluator.

log.subject: a burn rule for key 3 or key 5
log.why: Both are witnessed twice as non-burning (t3, t9 for key 3; t5, t7 for key 5); adding one would break replay immediately.

log.subject: the_burn_rules_lose_on_mdl_and_i_keep_them_anyway
log.why: Constraint 3 requires the conflict be stated: four rules for four pixels is one rule per pixel and a clear MDL loss; they are kept because they return eight transitions to scoring, and that is said rather than hidden.

log.subject: the_meter_reading_is_underdetermined_and_i_take_the_expressible_one
log.why: Clock (even command index) and primed-key both fit 9/9; the record does not separate them. I take the expressible one and name the separator: any press of key 3 or key 5 at an even index.

log.subject: the_burn_rules_cannot_fire_where_they_are_not_wanted
log.why: Written out as the exclusivity argument -- `below(?p) = wall' restricts to row 63, the two key-2 forms are mutually exclusive, and no panel cell in either configuration has a colour-1 cell to its right -- and certify's ambiguity check over 4 actions x 10 states is the test.

log.subject: the clock reading of the meter
log.why: I wanted `burn iff the command index is even'; the guard language has no counter and no state cell tracks parity. I wrote the primed-key rules instead and recorded the clock as a live rival reading in L-04 rather than pretending it lost.

log.subject: drawing the next burn at (63,59)
log.why: The cell has never changed, so it is board with no instance, and no rule can paint a first change. A second colour-9 type would be indistinguishable from Glyph9 and would double-claim cells. Recorded as a permanent one-burn lag, not a defect.

log.subject: obj0/obj1/obj5/obj6 (mdl_segmenter panel tracks)
log.why: Their frame ranges -- colour-1 block in frames 0-4, colour-2 ring from frame 5 for 2 frames, colour-1 ring from frame 7 for 3 -- date the toggle at t5 and t7 exactly as the panel rules do; no new type, since a second type on the same pixels double-claims them.

log.subject: obj3 (1006-cell colour-null blob)
log.why: connected_components(4) merged the maze floor with the body ring, so the segmenter cannot see the mover at all; its absence is the finding and it gets no declaration.

log.subject: obj4 (64-cell row-63 bar)
log.why: Already covered by the four Glyph9 instances at cols 60-63; the other 60 cells have never changed and are board.

log.subject: cegis_miner NoSeparatingGuard on transition 1
log.why: Correcting last round's reading: the miner's literal universe does not include the colour of the cell right of the burning edge, which is precisely the separator, so it found the edge of its own vocabulary and not a fact about the world -- and that misreading helped justify deleting a correct rule.

log.subject: cegis_miner verdict 'the world does not narrate as one mover'
log.why: True of the arm, false of the world: there is one rigid 24-pixel mover and the arm can only express 24 simultaneous recolours.

log.subject: zero_space global law over 75 cells
log.why: It enumerates exactly the dynamic census already in the manual, and the engine's own THIN verdict (rank 5 of 375 features) says it is unfalsified rather than confirmed.
